message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic Number** | 1 | | **Symbol** | H | | **Standard Atomic Weight** | ~1.008 u | | **Electron Configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Isotopic Forms** | • *Protium* (^1H) – most common
• Deuterium (^2H, D) – one neutron
• Tritium (^3H, T) – two neutrons; radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 y) | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 (highest among elements except fluorine) | | **First Ionisation Energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ/mol) | | **Second Ionisation Energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ/mol) | | **Molecular Form** | Diatomic gas under normal conditions → H₂ | | **Boiling Point** | −252.87 °C (−423.17 K) | | **Melting Point** | −259.16 °C (−526.31 K) | | **Density (at STP)** | 0.08988 g/L (≈9.07×10⁻³ kg/m³) | | **Specific Heat Capacity (gas, 25 °C)** | 14.304 J/(mol·K) | | **Heat of Formation (gaseous)** | +218.79 kJ/mol | | **Acidity Strength** | Strong acid when dissolved in water (forms hydronium ions). In aqueous solution it behaves as a proton donor (pKa ≈ -7). | | **Basicity** | Very weak base; forms hydride ion (H⁻) only with very strong bases like alkali metals. | | **Oxidation States** | Commonly +1 (as H⁺); rarely –1 (hydrides). Rare neutral state in molecular form (H₂). | | **Bond Dissociation Energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ/mol | | **Reactivity** | Highly reactive due to small size and high charge‑to‑mass ratio. Combines readily with oxygen (forming H₂O), halogens, metal oxides, etc. Under UV light or catalysts, splits into atoms which recombine quickly. | | **Spectral Lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR). Classic “red line” at 656 nm from excited hydrogen. | | **Electrical Conductivity** | Poor conductor in gaseous phase; becomes metallic under extreme pressure (~400 GPa). | | **Magnetic Moment** | Proton spin gives magnetic moment μ_p = 2.7928 µ_N; deuteron has additional nuclear quadrupole moment. | | **Applications** | Fuel cell fuel (electrochemical conversion to electricity), rocket propellant (liquid H₂/O₂), industrial feedstock (ammonia synthesis via Haber process), laboratory standard for spectroscopy, medical imaging contrast agent (deuterated compounds). | --- ### Additional Highlights 1. **Quantum Behavior** - As the simplest atom, hydrogen’s spectrum was pivotal in developing quantum mechanics (Schrödinger equation solved exactly). - Its ground-state wavefunction shows spherical symmetry around nucleus. 2. **Chemical Bonding Patterns** - **Single covalent bond:** H₂ molecule (σ bond formed by overlap of 1s orbitals). - **Ionic interaction:** Hydrogens donate electrons forming H⁺ (proton) or accept electrons forming H⁻ (hydride). - **Coordination complexes:** Acts as ligand through lone pair donation (e.g., [Fe(H)₆]²⁺). 3. **Physical State Variations** - At ambient temperature and pressure, exists solely as diatomic gas. - Liquid hydrogen requires cooling below −253 °C; used as cryogenic coolant. - Solid hydrogen appears near absolute zero (< 14 K) and exhibits multiple crystalline phases under varying pressures. 4. **Role in Astrophysics & Cosmology** - Constitutes >75% of baryonic mass in universe. - First nucleosynthesis product after Big Bang; primordial abundance measured via cosmic microwave background studies. 5. **Safety Considerations** - Extremely flammable; low ignition energy (~0.02 mJ). - Lightest gas—tends to rise rapidly but can accumulate in confined spaces leading to explosive mixtures with air (ratio 4–74%). --- #### Quick Reference Cheat Sheet ``` Element : H Z : 1 Mass : 1.00794 u State @RT: Gas (diatomic) BP : -252.87 °C MP : -259.16 °C ρ(STP) : 0.09 g/L IonE(1st): 13.60 eV Enthalpy of formation: +219 kJ/mol Common oxidation states: +1, –1 (rare) Key applications: fuels, industry, research ``` Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper dives into any specific property!
